subject: Reservation fallback guardrails & SLA alignment for Dedicated Nodes
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@oxpharm.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated reservation: fallback / crediting guardrails

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for taking this on. We're building out the inference surface for our ADAS drug-safety pipeline and want to make sure our Reserved GPU pool behaves predictably when traffic spikes or we have overnight batch runs. A few things we need clarity on before legal and procurement sign off: 

- If our Reserved pool becomes constrained, what is the automated fallback behavior? Specifically: which routes are preempted, how requests are routed to hosted/shared variants, and if there is a per-request or per-token crediting model for the time on fallback.
- How do you measure the Dedicated pool "availability" that would trigger fallback? Rolling window? 5m/1h/30d?
- Queueing behavior: do you expose priority lanes or tenant isolation so our long-running batch jobs do not starve interactive traffic?
- We need a runbook stub (who gets paged, escalation path, expected MTTR targets) and a sample SLA clause that lists uptime % and token latency percentiles used for credits.

I've attached an initial redline of your standard SLO language (OPH_SLA_DRAFT_v1.pdf) and a short spreadsheet of our expected daily QPS/peak sizes. Can we get a written proposal by EOD Monday (11/16)?

Thanks,
Samira
Samira Khan
Head of ML Ops
Oxford Pharmaceuticals
Attachment: OPH_SLA_DRAFT_v1.pdf (pdf, 142 KB)
Attachment: oph_expected_qps.csv (csv, 12 KB)

Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation: fallback / crediting guardrails

Samira — thanks for the clear list. Short answer: we can satisfy all of this, but the exact mechanics depend on the reservation profile you sign (hard reserve vs soft reserve) and the headroom tokens you buy. Below is our proposed approach and the concrete items we'll include in an updated SLA draft.

Proposal (summary):
- Fallback behavior: we will implement an automated fallback that routes excess traffic to a pinned hosted model variant (same architecture, quantized where needed) with a prioritized routing policy: interactive requests get priority over batch. Fallback is measured per-reserved-pool by a rolling 5m availability window with configurable grace (default 10m).
- Measurement and triggers: Dedicated pool availability = fraction of successful request slots not preempted over a rolling 5m window. A fallback trigger is: >5% of requests in that window were queued longer than configured concurrency threshold OR preempted.
- Crediting: if fallback duration for your pool exceeds 10 minutes in a given day, we will issue pro-rated token credits for the time beyond 10 minutes. Credits are computed on per-token spend during fallback and capped at your monthly committed spend.
- Queueing and priority lanes: Reserved pools support two priority bands — interactive and batch. Interactive gets preferential slots; batch jobs can be scheduled into low-priority slots or nightly windows. We also support KV-cache stickiness for interactive sessions to reduce tail latency after failovers.
- Runbook and escalation: we propose an ops runbook with 3-tier routing (oncall SRE -> Customer Reliability Manager -> Engineering lead) and MTTR targets: initial ack within 15 minutes, mitigation within 2 hours for degraded throughput.

I've drafted an updated SLA language and attached OPH_SLA_DRAFT_v2.pdf that captures these mechanics; Ben will add the technical quantization and concurrency recommendations. Can you confirm expected peak sequences (token length) and weekday spike profile? I want to make sure our headroom math aligns with your workload.

If this looks ok, let's schedule a 30-minute sync early next week to iron out the billing/credit formula and the contract wording.

Cheers,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
Attachment: OPH_SLA_DRAFT_v2.pdf (pdf, 128 KB)

From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation: fallback / crediting guardrails

Hi all — adding some technical specifics to make the SLA proposal actionable. I'm pasting the key runbook steps and assumptions; the attached CSV contains the sample reservation headroom calc for your numbers.

Key technical notes:
1) Queueing semantics: the runtime uses a per-pool token semaphore. Interactive band has N_interactive slots; batch band has N_batch slots. When pool occupancy would exceed N_total, requests are either queued up to a queue-time cap (default 30s) or routed to fallback. The routing decision is deterministic: interactive requests are queued first, batch requests can be immediately routed to fallback when under contention.

2) Cache stickiness: KV cache is sticky to the reservation and to session IDs where possible. During fallback we attempt best-effort cache rehydration on the hosted variant but there will be an initial cold-tail penalty on a per-session basis (we estimate +80–250ms on first few tokens for long contexts).

3) Fallback mapping: we will map your reserved model to a compatible hosted variant (same architecture; we may apply 4-bit quantization for cost parity). We include a per-request compatibility score in the routing decision; requests that require higher fidelity (long sequences, structured outputs) can be routed back to the reserved pool where possible.

4) Crediting calc (example): if fallback_duration_daily > 10m then credits = (fallback_duration_daily - 10m) / total_active_time * daily_reserved_cost. We'll expose the raw metrics (fallback_duration_daily, fallback_token_count, preempted_request_count) in Console.

5) Preserving compliance: traffic that touches PHI must not leave your VPC in Private deployments. For Hosted/Dedicated hybrid we will provide an option to route fallback only to dedicated regional hosts under a business-associate addendum; otherwise fallback could cross to shared infra.

Runbook (short):
- Detection: automated alert when preempted_request_count > 0.05 * last_5m_requests or avg_queue_time > 30s.
- Triage: oncall SRE attempt mitigation (scale/burst) within 15m.
- Escalation: escalate to SRE Pager, then to Eng Lead at 2h if no mitigation.
- Postmortem: RCA within 5 business days for incidents > 1h.

Attachment: reservation-metrics.csv (csv, 9 KB) — contains the headroom table I used for the sample numbers. Happy to walk through the calc on Monday.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation: fallback / crediting guardrails

Vanessa / Ben — this is very helpful, thank you. A couple of quick asks before we loop legal: 

- Can you add an explicit clause that in the event fallback routes traffic outside our contractual region (e.g., to a multitenant US cluster) there will be a notification and an alternate configuration that restricts fallback to regional dedicated hosts? We need this for our data governance team.
- Please confirm the crediting cap language; we don't want credits to exceed our committed spend but want a minimum floor for multi-hour outages.
- We require a 30-day advance notice for planned maintenance that could affect the reserved pool availability.

If you can incorporate those three items into OPH_SLA_DRAFT_v3 and share a final version, we can take it to procurement + legal this week and move to a scoping SOW. We're aiming to sign before end of month.

Thanks,
Oliver Price
Director, Infrastructure Engineering
Oxford Pharmaceuticals
